title: Steamtrain | Slight update and questions
author: Mediocre_Line7407
selftext:
Hello everyone, I am back with a small changelog of what I did since I showed my gameplay video a few weeks ago. Damn, that's weeks ago already.

**What's new**

I took many of the suggestions you all gave me and put them in. They were about the UI, the sounds, the graphics and some other little things. Thank you all for that. My game looks and sounds better now, and that makes me happier.

Obviously, I could just ask Claude to write me a changelog I can send here, but I do not want to.

In terms of gameplay, not much was added. The game got a small intro with a cinematic and a more straightforward tutorial. There are more tools now, in tiers, so the early tools are pretty weak and you want to make better ones. The train now takes damage on its journey and needs repairs. I also added quite a few models. I tried to add a player model too, but I just couldn't get it worked out with Claude for now. It was an idea of mine to make coop or multiplayer a thing, but I guess that is something for much later.

**Where I need your help**

My issue is world generation. I want story progression, but I also want to keep a generated world and a large research tree.

Colleagues suggested I look at how Satisfactory handles progression. In Voidtrain, probably the game most similar to mine, progression is fairly easy. Everything is in the void, so the environment has nothing to do with it. There are no tunnels, cliffs or anything else you have to cross. In my playthrough, progress depended fully on how far the research was. Once you had a certain research, the next area you teleported to held the next story element.

My world is different. It has tunnels, spiral climbs and cliffs, and I like the idea of exploring it. A demo, if I bring one out, would be free play, driving around, enjoying the scenery and doing a bit of research.

The full game should be one journey with a beginning, a middle and an end. It is not a roguelike. The research tree stays, the train goes forward and doesn't loop back to a base, and I would rather keep the world generated.

I see two ways and I am torn between them. One is a system that looks at what the player has researched and places the next obstacle and the next story moment on the line ahead, for example a climb the engine can't pull yet. The other is a hand built map, but then I would have to scrap my map generation and decide myself where every tunnel and climb goes.

So my question is this. How would you put story moments and obstacles that need research into a generated world, without teleporting to the next area like Voidtrain does? Have you seen a game that does this well? Should I go for a base you are heading back to?

Here is my older gameplay video, it is a bit outdated now, especially in terms of Ui, QoL and some research options: [https://youtu.be/z3PK8qLwi7k](https://youtu.be/z3PK8qLwi7k)
